newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Timorese protest in two towns in support of bishop.
newsitem.headline: Timorese protest in two towns in support of bishop.

text.p: More than 5,000 East Timorese staged peaceful demonstrations in two towns in the troubled territory on Thursday against Indonesian criticism of Nobel peace laureate Bishop Carlos Belo, police and residents said.

In the East Timor capital of Dili, crowds of mostly students marched on the governor's office to present a petition in support of Belo, while 300 others held a similar rally in Baucau, 100 km (60 miles) to the east.

"About 5,000 school and university students held a demonstration outside the governor's office, but it was orderly and there were no problems and no violence," East Timor's deputy police chief Colonel Atok Rismanto told Reuters by telephone.
"In Baucau around 300 people had a demonstration which was orderly. There was no one arrested," Rismanto said.
Demonstrators have held daily protests at the University of East Timor in Dili since Tuesday in support of Belo, who is highly respected in the mainly Catholic former Portuguese colony.
The bishop has been the focus of protests and media attacks in Jakarta for reportedly saying in a German magazine interview that Indonesian troops treated East Timorese like "dogs".
Hospital sources in Dili said two school-age sons of an East Timorese man who spoke at a Jakarta anti-Belo rally on Tuesday were treated in hospital on Wednesday after being beaten by youths.
The rally, in which demonstrators demanded Belo's expulsion from the country over his reported magazine remarks, was organised by youth groups aligned to the ruling Golkar party.

Rismanto said the protesters in Dili presented a petition on Thursday to a representative of Governor Abilio Soares, who is currently travelling in rural areas. Soares is due back in the seafront city on Friday.
Rismanto said both crowds dispersed without incident after midday. Other witnesses said there was no known confrontation between the students and security forces in either protest.
Residents said students and other demonstrators had gathered in the early morning outside the University of East Timor.
Some protesters carried banners saying "Viva, Bishop Belo".
Belo, who is in Jakarta attending an annual conference of Roman Catholic bishops, has refused to comment on the reported remarks carried in the German news magazine Der Spiegel.
The East Timor protests started on Tuesday, the fifth anniversary of the killing of at least 50 protesters by troops in Dili after a funeral for an anti-Indonesian activist.
Witnesses and human rights groups estimated at least 180 people died.
Indonesia invaded East Timor in December 1975 and declared the territory its 27th province the following July, a move not recognised by the United Nations.
Police said demonstrators broke some windows at the local legislature on Wednesday before moving on to the governor's seafront office, after which they dispersed peacefully.

Rismanto denied a Portuguese report that hundreds of demonstrators were detained in Baucau, nearby Laleia and Viqueque on the southern coast. Independent sources said they were aware of no arrests on Thursday.
Rismanto said he did not have reports of protests in other districts except for Dili and Baucau.
